svg.title: Round 3: four Weil-descent angles and what each measured
svg.text: Round 3: four Weil-descent angles, one ECDLP on E(F_{q^n})
ECDLP on E(F_{q^n})
rho: ≈ 0.886·√ℓ group ops
1 · decomposition over F_q (summation polys)
Part D: exact coverage, n = 2…5, odd and char 2
odd: Poisson, no structure (z ≤ 0.9)
char 2, n = 2: factor base in one coset of 2E
→ coverage 3/8, not 1 − e^{−1/2} (proved, M1–M3)
Arm D end to end: 2.7–66× rho in every cell
2 · prime fields: PKM tower factor bases
Kummer x↦x², Dickson split / torus, m = 2, 3
18 cells, ≥ 23 primes each
paired Poisson residual: |z| ≤ 1.84 everywhere
structure does not change coverage (P9 holds)
3 · n = 2: Res E ~ Jac(C), C genus 2 over F_p
Scholten-type C: x⁶f(κ/x) = κ³f(x); τ = φ* + σ(φ*)
first-cycle 2LP IC needs ≈ p/3 Jacobian ops, any h
rho needs ≈ 0.886·p/√h (h = cofactor ≥ 2 here)
control F: independent trials give the same p/3
ratio IC/rho over the pricing band: unresolved
(Jacobian op 41M+I measured vs 12M+I for E(F_{p²}))
4 · n = 4: genus-4 C with Jac(C) ~ Res_{F_{q⁴}/F_q} E
Theorem 5: q odd, n ≥ 3, C hyperelliptic ⇒ t even
so hyperelliptic covers never reach prime #E
q = 3 census, all genus 4: hyperelliptic 2187, non-hyp. 25515
(both masses match the literature counts)
9 non-hyperelliptic classes reach prime #E(F_81)
(t = 11, −1, −7, 9): Diem's q^{4/3} regime, toy size
